themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 5 this week compared to a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,233% increase (z-score: 9.55)—suggesting a sudden, coordinated campaign or systemic enforcement gap in CD 413 this week.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 9.55 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
This is the most extreme spike in the dataset by z-score
reporting_angles: Investigate whether a specific event (concert, rally, real estate campaign) triggered the surge or if enforcement has collapsed
Map the locations of illegal postings to identify geographic hotspots or neighborhoods being targeted

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 5 this week versus a baseline of 0.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 567% spike (z-score: 3.9)—raising concerns about mold, poor ventilation, or air contamination in residential buildings across the district.
evidence: 5 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline
567% increase with z-score of 3.9 (high severity threshold)
Timing coincides with winter heating season when mold and poor ventilation are common
reporting_angles: Interview residents filing complaints to understand whether the issue is concentrated in specific buildings or affects renters broadly
Investigate whether landlords are maintaining heating/ventilation systems or if cost-cutting is driving indoor air degradation

themes_detail.label: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Infrastructure Stress
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints rose to 14 last week versus a 6.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 133% increase (z-score: 3.88)—suggesting accelerating subsurface and surface deterioration in streets and sidewalks across the district.
evidence: 14 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.0 weekly average
Aligns with recurring community board budget requests for street reconstruction (submitted repeatedly, same request year after year)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint locations with DOT asset maps to identify worst-affected corridors and estimate repair backlog
Examine whether aging water mains are driving root intrusion into sewers, creating a cascading infrastructure problem

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 9 two weeks ago compared to a 2.1 per week baseline—a 324% spike (z-score: 3.9)—indicating possible unauthorized retail openings, operational complaints, or community resistance to legal cannabis businesses in CD 413.
evidence: 9 cannabis retailer complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.1 weekly average
Reflects tension between city legalization efforts and neighborhood concerns
reporting_angles: Identify which retailers are generating complaints and whether they have proper licensing or are operating illegally
Interview residents and community leaders about concerns: odor, traffic, youth access, or simply opposition to cannabis retail

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Spike
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints rose to 4 two weeks ago versus a 0.8 per week baseline—a 433% increase (z-score: 3.92)—suggesting potential industrial or environmental contamination, improper waste disposal, or a discrete incident in the district.
evidence: 4 hazardous materials complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average
Coincides with 16 full demolitions filed in the district over the last 90 days—potential source of asbestos, lead, or debris contamination
reporting_angles: Determine whether the spike correlates with specific demolition sites or industrial operations and whether EPA/DEC notifications were issued
Interview residents within complaint zip codes about symptoms (respiratory issues, odors, visible contamination) and timeline
